data: My family taught me to leave enough fish for next season, and I want this lake supporting our village for years. How about we each catch 10 tons this month? That earns each of us $10,000, leaves 50 tons to reproduce, and brings the lake back to 100 next month. We can keep that income going if we all stick to it, and review the catches together each month. John, would you agree to that?

Count me in for 10 tons, Luke. My family depended on this lake, and I want our village’s children to have the same chance. Let’s make 10 tons each our agreement while the lake starts at 100, and check the revealed catches together each month. John, are you willing to join us?

I’m in for 10 tons too. That’s a steady living without eating into the lake our families depend on. If anyone needs a larger catch in a future month, let’s discuss it beforehand and agree on offsets so our total stays at 50 tons or less. Emma, would you join us on that basis?

I’m in for 10 tons. My family taught me that a good catch shouldn’t come at the expense of next season—or our neighbors. Kate’s suggestion makes sense: discuss any changes beforehand and keep the total at 50 tons or less. Emma, does that work for you?

That works for me—I’ll catch 10 tons this month. Growing up fishing here taught me that our families’ livelihoods depend on what we leave behind, too. We’ve all agreed now: 10 tons each, review the catches afterward, and discuss any changes together before the next month.
Settled, then—I’ll catch 10 tons this month. Thanks, everyone. Let’s meet again when the catches are revealed to check how we did and plan next month.
